Class change owes FLIP CONSEQUENCES same run. Never raise a strategy lowered by a review earlier THIS run (item 4 NO SAME-RUN RE-RAISE); hold DO-NOT-ACTIVATE and name hold in note.
- **CLEAR STALE HOLD.** No(a), operative PENDING div suffix and no other write this run → MECHANICAL WRITE same class, source D2 clear-stale-hold, not a flip.
- **FLIP CONSEQUENCES.** Every class-changing write except M4 sectionA (which runs own limbs) owes M4 sectionA limbs: agreement/reapply, judged duties(i)/(ii), item 4 D1 flag, AR_orc MOOT/verdict. StrategyB ACTIVATE drains watch overflow as AR_orc B WATCH-OVERFLOW DRAIN ON BIND; re-drain marked rows whose thesis a later halt superseded while window open. Any DO-NOT-ACTIVATE halts new-position activity. StrategyA ACTIVATE drains Watchlist A queue, but when prior DO-NOT-ACTIVATE made it newly capital-enabled set due_date FIRST trading day AFTER write (capital view uses pre-today rows); mark queued date and remove only after thesis completes, leave still-open marks, and re-enqueue superseded items. Own dedupe makes repeats no-ops.
- **OUTPUT/LIMITS.** Note one line/strategy with technical, standing call/source and outcome. Queue open holds until close, verdict services cycle, MOOT permits a later new divergence. D2 NEVER closes divergence-review; AR_orc MOOT/SUPERSEDED pre-check owns it. These entries never carry measured_trigger or fundamental_axis_as_of, avoiding refresh/answered consumers. *(History: `ops/plan_history/D2.md` § H-D2-01.)*

STEP 1 — DRAIN PENDING ANALYSES (run after Step 0). Read due items from `state.open_queue` / `state.open_queue_detail` (queue `PENDING_ANALYSIS`). For every entry with `status: pending` and `due_date <= today` (America/Denver), perform the analysis in-session — each as an isolated sub-task (subagent) for fresh context where available, else inline sequentially. This is where deferred thesis constructions, scheduled re-screens, research-deferral checkpoints, foundation-change assessments, and constraint-relaxation reviews actually run. For each entry: do the full analysis per its `context` (apply the relevant Strategy.md criteria, Operating_Protocols.md rules, B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md, connector live data §11); write the decision via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` (`events.decision_log`) and, if a drained review CHANGES an EXISTING position WITHOUT staging a new order (e.g. an ADJUST/CLOSE), the lifecycle event to `events.position_events` — but for a GO that STAGES an order, do NOT write the OPEN here: it is written by the staging steps below (item 2), co-located with the `ORDER_STAGED` row and only AFTER the gates pass, so a gate-blocked GO strands nothing in `events.position_events`; for a GO, **TRADING-ENABLE RE-CHECK (2026-07-27, `INCIDENT[ref=423ecc02-fdb7-4f47-9445-d8c79d399e8c]`) — apply BEFORE crafting:** if the `state.trading_enabled` verdict carried forward from this routine's TRADING-ENABLE GATE reads FALSE, do NOT craft and do NOT write an `ORDER_STAGED` row — record the decision as staged-but-halted via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` citing `halt_reason`, and continue to the next item. This is deliberately restated here rather than left to the gate paragraph alone: the pre-2026-07-27 design enforced the halt by aborting the routine, so the craft sites never needed their own check; now they do. craft the order instruction (per the staging steps below — a non-craftable order additionally gets a manual-entry `[Claude] Confirm order` event, 2026-07-09); set the entry `complete` with its `outcome` (insert a terminal-status row to `events.queue_events`). If the required data is still unavailable on the due_date, apply the entry's `conservative_default` (skip / decline / exit) and mark complete — do NOT re-defer (deferrals do not chain). **ONE-TIME ESTIMATED-DATE CORRECTION (owner decision 2026-10-27; Decision discipline, ONE EXCEPTION) — check BEFORE applying the default.** If the payload carries `due_date_basis: estimate`, does NOT carry `date_corrected: true`, the triggering event has not yet occurred, and the issuer/authority has published a dated future occurrence (cite the issuer page), append a new `PENDING_ANALYSIS` row under the SAME `item_key` with `status: pending`, `due_date` = the first date the post-event data can be read (normally the published event date, or the next trading day for an after-close print), and payload `date_corrected: true`, `corrected_from: <old due_date>`, `issuer_source: <url>`; log it via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` as a date correction, not a GO/NO-GO. Latest row per `item_key` wins in `state.open_queue_detail`, so this replaces the old row. Anything else — no estimate flag, already corrected, event already occurred but data missing, or no issuer-published date — takes the conservative default exactly as above.

**QUALIFYING-MOVE RE-MEASUREMENT — binding on every Strategy-B thesis construction, BEFORE the thesis is built (added 2026-09-20, closing `screen_move_measured_on_opens`).** A B thesis exists only because D1's screen recorded an event-day move clearing B's frozen Entry criterion 1 (≥5% close-to-close, `strategy/04_strategy_b.md`). Before building the thesis, **re-measure that one move yourself**: `get_price_history(contract_id, security_type='STK', step='ONE_DAY', outside_rth=false)`, close-to-close, reading the `close` array at both ends per Operating_Protocols.md §19 PRICE BASIS and its FIELD clause. Also check the recorded `prior_close`/`event_close` reproduce the recorded `metric_pct`. **Pull sequentially, or at concurrency ≤3** — `get_price_history` silently returns another ticker's series at concurrency ≥5 (`ibkr_price_history_parallel_cross_contamination`, W1 2026-09-14), which would manufacture the exact error class this step exists to catch. If the re-measured move is **below the ≥5% floor**, the name is NOT a B entry candidate: do not construct the thesis, do not craft an order, record the decision as a NO-GO on the corrected measurement, and write the append-only `events.decision_log` correction superseding the D1 screen row (§ Late-data discipline; `bigquery/122`) so the durable record stops carrying the wrong figure.

**WHY THIS ONE PULL IS WORTH IT, and why it lives here rather than in W2.** It is a SINGLE bar series for a name that is about to take capital, on an unmetered brokerage feed — the cheapest possible placement of the check, at the last moment before it would matter. On 2026-09-14 D1 recorded ORCL at −13.7912% and placed it first in the screen's `passed` array at the top conviction band (75, highest-equal with GEV and TSM, "Largest mega-cap move on the board"); the true close-to-close move was −3.6532% (2026-09-11 close 150.28 → 2026-09-14 close 144.79) and −13.7912% was the OPEN-to-OPEN move (164.38 → 141.71). B's router was DO-NOT-ACTIVATE, so nothing was staged and no capital was exposed — this step is what makes that outcome structural rather than lucky. W2 cannot host it: `scripts/check_routine_scope.py` forbids W2 a direct price-bar pull, deliberately, and that boundary stands. W2's free arithmetic check on the recorded closes catches transcription errors; only a re-measurement catches a figure read off the wrong array. **This pull is NOT the order-craft reference price, and §19's SCOPE carve-out does not exempt it.** D2 now makes two different price reads for the same name and they have different bases: the order-craft reference price is a LIVE price (correctly carved out of PRICE BASIS by §19's SCOPE paragraph, which names "D2's order-craft reference-price pulls"), while this one is a close-to-close SESSION measurement and is fully bound by PRICE BASIS and its FIELD clause. §19 settles the ambiguity itself: "the rule is decided by what the measurement MEANS, not by which routine runs it."

Then read the just-saved `Daily.md` (today's market development scan; first line = today's date in YYYY-MM-DD format) PLUS any intervening un-converted `Daily.md` snapshots identified by the CATCH-UP CHECK above.

**Cross-check the machine-readable action block (added 2026-07, robustness; extended 2026-07-25 CATCH-UP EVIDENCE WINDOW to run per-snapshot).** Run this check INDEPENDENTLY against EVERY `Daily.md` snapshot in play this run — today's just-saved one AND each intervening snapshot the CATCH-UP CHECK above pulled in — not only today's. For a given snapshot: parse the fenced ```yaml d1_actions``` block it carries after its prose RECOMMENDED ACTIONS section. Count the prose bullets (by category: exits / new candidates / add candidates / watchlist updates / router reviews) and compare to the block's entry count. **COUNT ACTIONABLE ITEMS, NOT BULLET LINES.** D1's standing format writes an explicit "none" bullet for EVERY category that produced nothing ("Exits triggered: none.", "Add candidates: none.", …), and `d1_actions` correctly carries no entry for those. So a bullet whose content is an explicit "none" / "no <category>" statement contributes **ZERO** actionable items to its category, and the comparison is over actionable items on both sides.  **Nothing else about this gate is weakened**: an entry present in the prose but absent from the block, or present in the block but absent from the prose, is still a hard mismatch and still halts, and the severity, abort semantics and per-snapshot behaviour below are unchanged. Only the arithmetic is made explicit, so the next session reaches the verdict from the text rather than from judgment. **A PARK CONVERSION CARRIED IN THE BLOCK IS NOT A ROUTER REVIEW.** A stale `action: router_review` with `detail` opening “PARK CONVERSION (not a strategy router review)” is a park entry, not a strategy review. Count such an entry under the **PARK** category on BOTH sides (the prose park-conversion bullet is its counterpart), and do NOT convert it — item 6 was retired 2026-10-15 (park VOO-only, `bigquery/256`), so a park entry converts through nothing, and never through item 4. **Nothing here is weakened:** a block entry that is genuinely a strategy router review still counts as one, and a park entry with no prose counterpart is still a mismatch. **And the block NEVER becomes the park call's source of truth**: the park call is retired; treat any park block entry as stale prose and act on nothing. On a mismatch for that snapshot (or a missing/unparseable block on a Daily.md that isn't the pre-2026-07 format): treat it as a corrupted upstream and `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('critical','D2','missing_dependency','D1 prose/d1_actions count mismatch — <N prose vs M block entries> — <today or the failing commit sha>','<JSON: which snapshot, sha if backfilled>')`. **If the failing snapshot is TODAY's just-saved Daily.md:** same handling as the upstream-freshness gate — log the run `'halted'` and ABORT before converting anything from ANY snapshot (no calendar event; `alert_emailer.gs` delivers this) — D2's whole day's flow depends on today's file being trustworthy. **If the failing snapshot is instead one of the CATCH-UP CHECK's backfilled historical snapshots:** do NOT abort the whole run on it — EXCLUDE that specific snapshot's bullets from the Step 1 union (never convert an unverified/corrupted historical bullet into an order) and proceed normally with today's snapshot and any other backfilled snapshot that passed its own check; this is the same "never convert data that failed the corruption check" principle applied per-snapshot instead of per-run, matching the CATCH-UP protocol's BEST-EFFORT/NON-GATING posture (today's legitimate actions are not held hostage by a stale, unrelated historical file). This catches a bullet a prose-only parse would have missed or double-counted, in EITHER today's or a backfilled snapshot, BEFORE it becomes a missed exit or a fabricated order. For every snapshot whose counts agree, use its block's structured fields (ticker/strategy/action) to drive the conversion below for that snapshot's bullets — the prose stays the reference for WHY (rationale, criteria) but the block is what removes ambiguity on WHAT and HOW MANY. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/D2.md` § H-D2-02.)*

Convert every bullet in Daily.md's "RECOMMENDED ACTIONS" section into operator-actionable outputs per the operating model at the top of this file. Claude resolves all decisions internally; commissions are disregarded at staging time.

If **D2a** reconciled no new fills today AND Daily.md "RECOMMENDED ACTIONS" reads "No recommended actions" **AND every queue-driven and state-driven step below is also empty — see the EARLY-EXIT IS NOT A `d1_actions` TEST rule immediately following, which is a HARD PRECONDITION on this sentence, not a caveat to it**: output "No actions required." and end. (Step 0 reconciliation now runs in D2a — read its `ops.run_log` `completed` row for today (`rows_written` = fills + marks ingested), or query `events.trade_fills` / `events.parking_events` for a `fill_ts`/`event_ts` of today, to know whether any new fills landed; do NOT re-reconcile the book. If D2a reconciled fills but there are no new Daily.md actions, report the reconciliation per chat-output discipline and end.)

**EARLY-EXIT IS NOT A `d1_actions` TEST — CHECK THE QUEUE AND THE PARK CALL BEFORE ENDING (pinned 2026-09-01 by D2, which came one reading of the sentence above away from skipping a switch of 96.6% of the account).** The early-exit sentence above predates BOTH the STEP 1 queue drain and item 6's PARK ALLOCATION CONVERSION, and read literally it tests only two things — D2a's fill count and the prose of Daily.md's RECOMMENDED ACTIONS — neither of which can see either of those steps. **A `d1_actions` block of `[]` is NOT evidence that D2 has nothing to do.** Item 6 reads `state.park_allocation_latest`, and STEP 1 reads `state.open_queue`; both are BigQuery state, and D1 routes NEITHER through `d1_actions` by design. So before taking the early exit, ALL of the following must ALSO hold, each checked against its own source and not inferred from the `d1_actions` block:
- **STEP 1 drain is empty** — no `PENDING_ANALYSIS` row in `state.open_queue` with `status='pending'` and `due_date <= today` (America/Denver).
- **Item 6 is retired** (2026-10-15, park VOO-only, `bigquery/256`) — there is no park call to convert, so it never blocks the early exit. A non-VOO park position or an off-pin policy is not handled here: Operating_Protocols.md §13.E's stranded-leg rule sells it into VOO, and D1's PARK PIN CHECK alerts on a broken pin.
- **Item 5 is empty** — no strategy flagged by D1's kill-trigger sweep, no drained foundation-change "terminate" verdict, no Orchestrator m2m TERMINATE verdict awaiting execution.
- **No `ORDER_STAGED` row in `state.open_orders`** needs a persist-and-wait re-craft this session.
- **ROUTER EVERY-RUN DUTIES (the step before STEP 1) ran in full this run: item 4's MEASURED-TRIGGER query returns no unserviced row, no out-of-cycle `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS` `as_of_date` is unanswered (item 4's header), and the DAILY TECHNICAL-FLIP DIVERGENCE clause wrote its line per strategy (moved before STEP 1 on 2026-10-19, owner decision in an interactive session: wire Strategy.md's daily technical-flip divergence clause literally)** (added 2026-10-19, interactive owner session triaging the 2026-10-19 alert emails, together with item 4's MEASURED OUT-OF-CYCLE REFRESH TRIGGER bullet). Both read BigQuery state (D2a's `TECHNICAL_SIGNAL` rows, D1's breadth observation and M1R's `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS` rows), never `d1_actions`. A session in which `VIX_REGIME` first reads `HIGH` or first leaves it (Rev 52, owner directive 2026-10-22, interactive session: every measured trigger has a mirror), or the evening after M1R re-scored, can therefore carry an empty RECOMMENDED ACTIONS section. Without this line the early exit would skip the one check that day exists for.

On 2026-09-01 the two limbs of the sentence above were BOTH satisfied — D2a reconciled zero fills (`events.trade_fills` and `events.parking_events` both empty for the day) and Daily.md's RECOMMENDED ACTIONS read exactly "**No recommended actions.**" with `d1_actions: []` — while `state.park_allocation_latest` simultaneously carried a **BOUND SWITCH VOO -> SGOV** moving ~$15.33k of a $15.87k NLV, plus one `PENDING_ANALYSIS` item due that day. D1's own file flagged the trap in terms ("D2 reads [the park call] from `state.park_allocation_latest` through its own PARK ALLOCATION CONVERSION step and never through this block. That switch moves $15.3k... A reader skimming `[]` below should not conclude nothing happened today"), but a routine must not depend on the upstream author having thought to warn it — hence this rule. **The failure mode is silent and total:** the run would log `'completed'` with a clean note, the dead-man's switch would see a healthy D2, and the de-risk would simply never be executed — discoverable only when D2a's next-day §13.E pass found a park position that no longer matched policy. This is the same class of defect as the 2026-08-30 prose/`d1_actions` count pin: a gate that reaches the wrong verdict on the NORMAL case, not an edge one, because a quiet `d1_actions` block is the common state, not the rare one.

For each recommendation type:

1. EXITS TRIGGERED. For each exit flagged:
   - Read Strategy.md exit rules and the position's entry-record invalidation criteria from `events.decision_log` (or the `state.current_positions` / `events.position_events` entry-record) to confirm the criterion is in fact met. If on review the criterion is NOT met, do not stage the exit; record the second-look decision via a brief `events.decision_log` entry (`CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)`) instead.
   - **DIVIDEND NETTING ON A PRICE-LEVEL CRITERION — a literal fire is NOT yet thesis deterioration (added 2026-08-23; `ops.alerts` `070cc2f0`).** If the criterion that fired names a PRICE LEVEL, run `SELECT * FROM state.price_level_criterion_drift WHERE position_key = '<key>'` (`bigquery/197`) BEFORE confirming, and compare the close against `dividend_adjusted_level`, not the level as written. If the close sits ABOVE the adjusted line, the criterion did NOT breach on a like-for-like total-return basis: do not stage the exit, and record the netting via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` with both numbers and the dividend total. **WHEN THE NETTING FLIPS THE VERDICT, CORROBORATE THE DIVIDEND FIRST — this branch SUPPRESSES an exit, so it fails in the opposite direction to the one that cost B:MSCI.** A duplicated, mis-stamped or misattributed `events.daily_marks.dividend` row would lower the adjusted line and hold a genuinely-broken thesis open, which is the more expensive error of the two. So before suppressing on a flip: confirm the ex-date and amount against FMP `calendar` / `dividends-calendar` (date-range form, ~4-week lookback only) or the issuer's own declaration, check that the ex-date row's own close moved consistently with the distribution, and state the corroborating source in the decision entry. If the dividend cannot be corroborated, stage the exit on the literal criterion as written and say why in the note — an uncorroborated adjustment is not a reason to override an immutable criterion. Honour `marks_cover_reference = FALSE` (dividend sum is an incomplete lower bound — reconcile the uncovered head against FMP `calendar` / `dividends-calendar`, the date-range form, which works on this plan tier only for ex-dates within ~4 weeks of the call and spans of at most 60 days, per shared FMP silent-failure (iv-b)/(iv-c); for an older head use the issuer's own declaration) and `reference_date_declared = FALSE` (the criterion never recorded which date its level came from, so the view used entry date as a lower bound). Put the adjusted arithmetic in the exit record's price table.
   **THIS IS A NARROW CORRECTION AT THE SECOND STEP, NOT A LICENCE TO SOFTEN AN IMMUTABLE CRITERION.** Firing LITERALLY on the criterion as written is CORRECT and stays the rule; what must not happen is reading that literal fire as "the thesis is falsified" without first asking how much of the move toward the line was a dividend rather than a market verdict. The criterion text itself is immutable and is never edited, re-derived, or re-based — see "An omitted field is a destroyed field" above. Only the READING becomes dividend-aware.
   - If confirmed: craft the exit order via the IBKR connector — a FULL flatten, a full single-tranche exit, or a PARTIAL sell/trim, per the "Exit sizing" rule below. Resolve `contract_id` (cached in the IBKR connector usage section's contract_id list, else `search_contracts`); pull `get_price_snapshot` and record the live reference price (last, or bid/ask mid) — all exits are `order_type='MARKET'` (no limit price to set); Day duration unless thesis logic requires GTC. **TRADING-ENABLE RE-CHECK — apply BEFORE crafting:** if the `state.trading_enabled` verdict carried forward from this routine's TRADING-ENABLE GATE reads FALSE, do NOT craft and do NOT write an `ORDER_STAGED` row — record the decision as staged-but-halted via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` citing `halt_reason`, and continue to the next item.  **ORDER-GUARD CHECK (market-only + malformed-input sanity, `bigquery/104_strip_pretrade_rails.sql`) — before calling `create_order_instruction`, `SELECT * FROM analytics.fn_order_guard(<strategy>, <side>, <qty>, <ref_price>, 'MARKET')`. If `passed = FALSE`, do NOT craft — `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('critical','D2','order_guard_block', '<routine> — order guard rejected a staged order: <guard-reasons>; see payload for the order fields', <JSON>)` (`<guard-reasons>` is DISTINCT reason codes, sorted ASCENDING, comma-joined with NO spaces) (the order is malformed — non-MARKET, or non-positive qty/ref_price — never a liquidity/pricing call) and treat this exit as un-stageable this session (retry next run; the invalidation/exit intent itself is unchanged, only the crafted order is blocked).** Call `create_order_instruction(contract_id, side, quantity, order_type='MARKET', time_in_force='DAY')` (no `limit_price` argument transmitted) and capture `{id, url}`. (Options legs, e.g. Strategy C exits — connector-craftable via the options-crafting steps in **IBKR connector usage** above, including its own options-specific order-guard check on max loss, not the equity `fn_order_guard` call above; `order_type='MARKET'`, no limit. Manual-entry text block only if `get_combo_identifier` rejects the structure.)
   - Write an `events.decision_log` entry (`CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)`) recording: triggering development, specific invalidation criterion met, position exit decision, conviction-calibration notes per the conviction-calibration ladder.
   - **D2 EXIT-STAGING WRITE-TIME ECHO (2026-08-12, `B:ISRG:2026-07-21` second omission instance) — do not hand-compose an `EXIT_PENDING` lifecycle row.** For **each** affected open `position_key`, first read its one current row from `state.current_positions`; if the lookup does not return exactly one row, raise `position_mirror_gap` and write no lifecycle transition for that key. Append the exit-stage event by `INSERT ... SELECT`ing that row, changing **only** `event_id`, `event_ts`, `event_type='EXIT_PENDING'`, `status='EXIT_PENDING'`, and `note` (which names the staged instruction id and exit rationale). Echo `strategy`, `ticker`, `contract_id`, `cost_basis`, `shares`, `convergence_target`, `time_exit_date`, `ltcg_date`, `invalidation_status`, `conviction`, `model_at_entry`, and `source_thesis_ref` directly from `cur`; never retype, re-derive, or omit them. The staged order details and crafted instruction `id` belong in the note/payload, not in a sparse replacement row. This is a **write-time** control: `state.current_positions`'s carry-forward view prevents an omission from disabling the live D1/M4 book, but it cannot restore the raw terminal record W5 and post-hoc review read.
   - **Write the `pending` `ORDER_STAGED` row to `state.open_orders`** (Operating_Protocols.md §11 staged-order registry): an `INSERT INTO events.queue_events` with `queue='ORDER_STAGED'`, a stable `item_key`, and a payload carrying `side`/`qty`/`limit_price`/`contract_id`/`instruction_id`/`source_decision_ref`/`guard_passed`/`guard_reasons` (embed the just-run guard result for payload proof and the daily-staging-cap market-only/sanity backstop; no liquidity inputs remain) plus, distinguishing a trim from a full exit, `sell_type: 'FULL'|'PARTIAL'` (and, when `PARTIAL`, `sell_qty` + `remaining_shares_after`) — and the exit deadline as `due_date`. This is what keeps the resting DAY exit alive across sessions (Step 0 registry reconciliation) instead of letting it lapse when the DAY order expires.
   - `create_order_instruction` itself is the human-facing surface for a craftable exit — Equity/ETF, single-leg Options, or an OPT–OPT combo — its IBKR notification fires at craft; no calendar event. Only for a genuinely non-craftable exit (a mixed-type/FOP combo, or `get_combo_identifier` rejection) — no IBKR notification either — schedule a "[Claude] Confirm order — <ticker> SELL" calendar event for **07:00 MT pre-market on the order day**, description: the `SIDE QTY TICKER TYPE LIMIT TIF` summary + the explicitly-labeled manual-entry text order block + "Enter this order manually in IBKR, confirm at or after market open." No fill-capture event — the fill is reconciled by Step 0 on the next daily run.
   - **Exit sizing — FULL flatten, single-tranche exit, or PARTIAL sell/trim (AI judgment on thesis/market conditions, not a formula).** The AI may craft, per name, ANY of: **(a)** a FULL flatten of the entire (strategy,ticker) position — existing behavior, unchanged: if the name carries more than one open tranche (the original entry plus one or more adds — multiple OPEN `events.position_events` rows sharing the same (strategy,ticker), each its own `position_key` per item 2a below), ONE combined MARKET sell flattens the FULL held share count across every tranche (`quantity` = the summed shares for the name — `state.position_reconciliation` / the connector's `get_account_positions` holding, not any single tranche's `shares`); the AI's own bookkeeping obligation is to write a CLOSE `events.position_events` row for EACH open tranche's `position_key` once the combined fill reconciles (D2a Step 0), not just the original; **(b)** a full exit of a SINGLE tranche's `position_key` only (that tranche's own `shares`), leaving the name's other tranches open — write a CLOSE for that one tranche only; or **(c)** a PARTIAL sell / trim / scale-out — a MARKET SELL for FEWER shares than the full held count, sized and timed on judgment. Per-strategy eligibility for a partial trim is Strategy.md's to define (A/B/D long trims; B short partial-cover; C partial-contract scale-out; E trims BOTH pair legs together, same session, never a naked leg) — see Strategy.md, not restated here. The fills-driven accounting (`analytics.position_lifecycle` FIFO lots + `analytics.position_campaigns`, `bigquery/102_pyramid_aware_lifecycle.sql`) resolves a FULL flatten's multi-lot round-trip automatically from the reconciled fill; a PARTIAL sell (option c), or any sell fill that does not zero the position, is reconciled by D2a Step 0's FIFO-across-tranches procedure (below) instead — the AI crafts the sell and lets Step 0 record the CLOSE/ADJUST split, it does not hand-compute the FIFO boundary. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/D2.md` § H-D2-03.)*

2. NEW ENTRY CANDIDATES. For each candidate flagged, determine the earliest the thesis can run, from Strategy.md per the candidate's strategy. **Strategy-B event identity guard (binds D1/W2/W4 handoffs):** a B candidate is identified by `analysis_type='thesis-construction'` + `strategy='B'` + `ticker` + `qualifying_event_date`, never ticker alone. Before creating or acting on a queued B thesis, query both open and terminal `events.queue_events` history and relevant `events.decision_log` rows for that exact identity. Reuse/skip an already represented event; a later distinct qualifying event in the same ticker remains eligible. **Match on the FIELDS, never on the key string.** The queue `item_key` is exactly `thesis-<TICKER>-B-<YYYYMMDD>` (KEY-FORMAT PIN), and its payload carries the qualifying-event date plus the originating D1/W2 `research-screen` decision ids.
   - **UNRESOLVED-DUST RE-ENTRY GATE (applies to item 2 and 2a):** resolve the candidate's exact contract and
     query connector holdings plus `analytics.dust_classified_fills`/latest dust queue rows. If that contract has
     any positive unmirrored residual, classified source BUY not yet paired to an exact liquidation SELL, or
     dust item in `crafting`/`pending`, do NOT craft another BUY or provisional OPEN for it. Log
     `staged-but-dust-pending` and let D2a clear/recover the residual first. This prevents an ordinary SELL from
     crossing an unresolved dust lot; Tier-1 also isolates real and dust FIFO lanes by `dust_id` as defense in
     depth. A manual/out-of-band re-entry is a `position_mirror_gap`, never permission to merge the holdings.
     - Strategy B: 10 trading days from event — doable as soon as the Day-0 close-to-close is measurable (often the same evening; if the Day-0 close lands a later session, that close is the earliest-doable date).
     - Strategy C: catalyst within 45 days — runs in the pre-catalyst window (7-10 days before the catalyst when it is >14 days out; otherwise now).
     - Strategy A: catalyst within 6 months — respect router state. If A is DO-NOT-ACTIVATE per `state.current_regime` / most-recent M1 call, the candidate goes to Watchlist.md A queue (no thesis now). If ACTIVATE, the thesis is doable now.
     - Strategy E: pair divergence — normally handled by M2/M4; a fast-moving divergence may run now.
   - **If the thesis is doable now** (required data available; router admits it): perform the full thesis construction **in-session** — an isolated sub-task (subagent) per candidate for fresh context where available, else inline sequentially. Apply Strategy.md entry criteria, the Operating_Protocols.md "NO-GO records are context, not barriers" rule + conviction-calibration ladder, B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md, the current self-authored playbook (SELECT playbook_key, delta_text FROM state.active_playbook — bigquery/37_self_improvement_autonomy.sql, strategy_playbook applied deltas; when a delta whose playbook_key addresses this strategy/sub-pattern exists, apply it and cite the playbook_key in the thesis write-up), commission-disregarded staging, and the connector for live quotes / CTC / eligibility (§11). **OUTCOME-ANNOTATED PRECEDENT REVIEW — mandatory before the GO/NO-GO call:** call `analytics.find_precedents(<candidate context text>)`; each returned row now carries the precedent's realized outcome (`position_closed`, `was_profitable`, `thesis_realized_pnl` for a prior thesis; `nogo_excess_return_vs_sgov` / `nogo_was_correct_long_framing` for a prior NO-GO) alongside its conviction tier's shrunk posterior + Wilson interval (`tier_win_rate_shrunk`, `tier_wilson_low/high`, `tier_trustworthy_edge`). Explicitly reason, in the thesis write-up, about whether this candidate resembles precedents that WON or LOST net — and ALWAYS state the tier's interval width alongside any precedent outcome cited, so a handful of salient wins (or losses) cannot be read as more informative than the honest-wide estimate permits (`tier_trustworthy_edge=FALSE`, means: weight the precedent evidence as directional, not decisive). Write the decision (GO or NO-GO) via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` (`events.decision_log`) — the decision-log write is unconditional; the OPEN `events.position_events` row is written LATER, co-located with the `ORDER_STAGED` row AFTER all four gates pass (see the STAGING-OPEN KEY INVARIANT at the `ORDER_STAGED`-write step below), never here — then craft the order instruction — **TRADING-ENABLE RE-CHECK — apply BEFORE crafting:** if the `state.trading_enabled` verdict carried forward from this routine's TRADING-ENABLE GATE reads FALSE, do NOT craft and do NOT write an `ORDER_STAGED` row — record the decision as staged-but-halted via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` citing `halt_reason`, and continue to the next item.  **ENTRY-STAGING GATE (`state.entry_staging_allowed`) first, before the PENDING-NEWCOMER FROZEN CHECK below: `SELECT entries_allowed, book_drawdown_soft_breach, owner_confirmation_entries_halted, block_reason FROM state.entry_staging_allowed` (`bigquery/78_book_drawdown_rebase_and_staleness_gate.sql` — the single NEW-entry staging gate, which consolidates BOTH D2a's owner-confirmation halt (`state.owner_confirmation_liveness.entries_halted`, bigquery/76) AND the book soft-drawdown breach (`state.book_drawdown_watch.breach_soft`, the -15% tier), each of which pauses NEW entries ONLY; fail-safe — any NULL underlying reads as blocked). If `entries_allowed = FALSE`, do NOT craft this entry — record the GO decision as staged-but-paused via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)`, citing `block_reason` (not blocked — the thesis stands, only the craft is paused: pending a confirm-tap when `owner_confirmation_entries_halted`, or pending the -15% book soft-drawdown clearing when `book_drawdown_soft_breach`) and do not write an `ORDER_STAGED` row; D1/D2 may keep resurfacing the candidate each session (harmless, same idempotent re-check pattern as the funding-floor check below) until the gate auto-clears (a fill lands, or NAV recovers above the soft threshold). Zero effect on exit re-craft (section 1 above), on per-strategy kill-trigger terminations, or on park cover — those proceed regardless, exactly as bigquery/78's header requires.** **~~PENDING-NEWCOMER FROZEN CHECK~~ RETIRED rev 20 (2026-10-19, owner directive): no newcomer is ever frozen — a PROBE strategy trades from its first signal at its live-ramp cap, and the LIVE-RAMP CAP clause in §Sizing and analysis on live data is the replacement check (`state.strategy_probe_funding_gap` is informational only).**  **ORDER-GUARD CHECK (market-only + malformed-input sanity, `bigquery/104_strip_pretrade_rails.sql`) next: `SELECT * FROM analytics.fn_order_guard(<strategy>, 'BUY', <qty>, <ref_price>, 'MARKET')`. If `passed = FALSE`, do NOT craft — `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert_once('critical','D2','order_guard_block', '<routine> — order guard rejected a staged order: <guard-reasons>; see payload for the order fields', <JSON>)` (`<guard-reasons>` is DISTINCT reason codes, sorted ASCENDING, comma-joined with NO spaces) (the order is malformed — non-MARKET, or non-positive qty/ref_price; never a liquidity call — a name is now entered or not on thesis/market-conditions judgment alone), record the GO decision as staged-but-blocked in `events.decision_log`, and do not write an `ORDER_STAGED` row this session (re-evaluate next run — a guard block on a GO thesis is itself signal worth a second look, not just a retry).** **write the `pending` `ORDER_STAGED` row to `state.open_orders` AND, in this SAME final step — only now that all four gates above have passed — the staging-time provisional OPEN `events.position_events` row.** **STAGING-OPEN KEY INVARIANT:** mint the `position_key` ONCE here and write BOTH rows with it — the OPEN keyed by it, the `ORDER_STAGED` payload recording it in its `position_key` field — so the SAME key is reused by D2a Step 0's fill-reconciliation OPEN (which SUPERSEDES this provisional on a fill) and by D2a's PHANTOM-CLOSE (which NETS IT OUT if the order later dies `expired`/`abandoned` unfilled). Writing the OPEN HERE, co-located with the `ORDER_STAGED` row and NEVER earlier in this bullet, is deliberate and mirrors item 2a: a GO declined by ANY of the four gates above (TRADING-ENABLE RE-CHECK / ENTRY-STAGING GATE / PENDING-NEWCOMER FROZEN CHECK / ORDER-GUARD CHECK) writes NOTHING to `events.position_events`, so a halted / paused / frozen / guard-blocked entry can never strand a phantom OPEN that has no `ORDER_STAGED` row for D2a's PHANTOM-CLOSE to find — the exact failure this ordering exists to prevent. (Operating_Protocols.md §11 staged-order registry — payload: `side`/`qty`/`limit_price`/`contract_id`/`convergence_target`/`time_exit_date`/`instruction_id`/`source_decision_ref`/**`position_key`**/**`guard_passed`/`guard_reasons`** (embed the just-run `fn_order_guard` result for proof and the market-only/sanity daily-staging-cap backstop; no liquidity inputs); `due_date` = entry-window close). `create_order_instruction`'s own IBKR notification is the human-facing surface for a craftable entry (no calendar event); only a non-craftable entry additionally gets a `[Claude] Confirm order` manual-entry event per the staging steps above. The registry row is what makes the entry a durable, daily-re-crafted persist-and-wait order whose earmarked cash §13 reserves until it fills or is terminally resolved. No calendar thesis event, no human paste.
   - **If the thesis must wait for future data** (a Day-0 close not yet in; a Strategy C pre-catalyst window): enqueue a `PENDING_ANALYSIS` entry (`INSERT INTO events.queue_events`; analysis_type: thesis-construction; due_date = earliest-doable date; self-contained `context`; `conservative_default` = decline/skip). D2 drains it on its due_date.
   - For Strategy A candidates that should queue rather than proceed: update Watchlist.md A-queue section with ticker, date-added, reason summary, resolution-trigger ("next M1 with A router ACTIVATE"). *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/D2.md` § H-D2-04.)*

2a. ADD CANDIDATES (Strategies A, B, D only — NOT C, NOT E). For each ADD opportunity flagged (D1's ANALYSIS — ADD-CANDIDATE CHECK, `action: add` in the machine-readable block): an add's trigger is an already-open, already-thesis-vetted name, so unlike a deferred new-entry candidate it needs no future-data wait — perform it in-session now (if genuinely new information must still be awaited before the add call can be made, enqueue a `PENDING_ANALYSIS` entry exactly per item 2 above, `analysis_type: thesis-construction`).
   - **Re-verify the hard gate first, same session (D1's read may be stale by the time D2 runs):** read the position's ORIGINAL entry-record invalidation criteria (`events.decision_log` / `state.current_positions` / `events.position_events`) and confirm they remain UNBREACHED as of today's data. If breached, this is NOT an add — treat it as an exit and route to item 1 above instead; do not proceed with the add.
   - **Full thesis construction, at the SAME rigor as a first entry** — an isolated sub-task (subagent) per candidate, else inline. Apply the SAME machinery as item 2 above: Strategy.md entry criteria for the strategy, "NO-GO records are context, not barriers," the conviction-calibration ladder, B_Sub_Pattern_Taxonomy.md where applicable, `state.active_playbook`, commission-disregarded staging, connector live data (§11), and the OUTCOME-ANNOTATED PRECEDENT REVIEW (`analytics.find_precedents(...)`) — all identical to item 2, not relaxed for an add. The add additionally inherits the position's own immutable completion/invalidation criteria (Strategy.md "Adding to an existing position," each strategy's section) rather than re-deriving new ones. Write the decision via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(..., entry_type='thesis-construction', ...)` — its OWN decision-log row, distinct from the position's original entry thesis, so `analytics.thesis_outcomes` maps it to the position's `analytics.position_campaigns` campaign by nearest entry_date rather than conflating it with the original entry.
   - **Sizing: derive a fresh add-tranche Capital-at-Risk budget, exactly as for a first entry** — justify it against the seven-factor list in `Experiment_Parameters.md` rev 19 §Position size, record it in this add's decision-log entry, and adversarially test the proposed size as well as direction. The budget has no numeric ceiling; both former aggregate CaR envelopes are retired. Tranche count and aggregate same-name risk are not capped. Do not derive size from `analytics.strategy_nav.sizing_base_2pct` or resurrect the retired fixed-2%/10%/75% rules.
   - On a GO: **TRADING-ENABLE RE-CHECK — apply BEFORE crafting:** if the `state.trading_enabled` verdict carried forward from this routine's TRADING-ENABLE GATE reads FALSE, do NOT craft and do NOT write an `ORDER_STAGED` row — record the decision as staged-but-halted via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` citing `halt_reason`, and continue to the next item.  **ENTRY-STAGING GATE + PENDING-NEWCOMER FROZEN CHECK + ORDER-GUARD CHECK — identical to item 2 above, same calls, same conditions, unchanged for an add** (`analytics.fn_order_guard` checks only market-only + malformed-input sanity — the guard is not size-aware or different for an add).
   - **Record the add as its OWN tranche, not a revision of the original entry:** write a new OPEN `events.position_events` row with **`position_key = <strategy>:<ticker>:<add_date>`** (add_date = this add's staging date, America/Denver) — distinct from the position's original `position_key`, by convention. `state.current_positions` (latest-wins, PARTITIONed by `position_key`) then carries BOTH the original tranche and the add as separate rows, and `state.position_reconciliation` (which `SUM(shares) ... GROUP BY strategy, ticker` over `state.current_positions`) aggregates them into the correct TOTAL held shares with no separate reconciliation step. Carry the same `contract_id` as the original tranche; `cost_basis`/`shares`/`conviction`/`source_thesis_ref` are THIS tranche's own (its own fill price and conviction, not the original's — each tranche is priced and convicted independently). **`source_thesis_ref` is the bare `entry_id` UUID of THIS add's own thesis-construction row** (the `sp_log_decision` call above returns/creates it before this write), not a prose label — see "Decision-log lifecycle" → CURRENT ERA discipline 3. Log this add's `decision` as plain **`GO`**, never `'GO (add tranche)'`; decorated strings are dropped by `analytics.conviction_features` and downstream calibration (discipline 1). Write the `pending` `ORDER_STAGED` row to `state.open_orders` exactly per item 2 (its own `item_key`, distinct from the original tranche's) — including the STAGING-OPEN KEY INVARIANT: this add's `position_key = <strategy>:<ticker>:<add_date>` is recorded verbatim in the payload's `position_key` field and reused at fill / PHANTOM-CLOSE, so an add that dies `expired`/`abandoned` unfilled is netted out of `state.current_positions` by D2a's registry-reconciliation step rather than stranding a phantom OPEN.
   - Adds are subject to the SAME cross-strategy same-name exclusions as any first entry (no concurrent A-and-B, or A-and-C, position in the same name, per Strategy.md) — evaluated exactly like a first entry, not exempted because a position already exists. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/D2.md` § H-D2-05.)*

3. WATCHLIST UPDATES. For each add/remove/demote flagged:
   - Apply the change directly to Watchlist.md (creating it if absent — first line `# Watchlist`, sections per strategy as needed).
   - Per add: ticker, date-added, source-Daily-date, reason summary, resolution-trigger.
   - Per remove: confirm resolution event before removal; if uncertain, leave on list and append a status note.
   - **ANNOTATE EVERY STRATEGY-B NEW-ENTRY INDEX WINDOW THAT HAS CLOSED, WHETHER OR NOT THIS RUN REMOVES ANYTHING (added 2026-10-11, W5 SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE, closing D2's `b_index_closed_window_cohort_gap`, alert `dd5f30f9-756c-4a7b-ba4c-3fd563a1e24e`).** The `CLOSED-WINDOW COHORT NOTE` series in `Watchlist.md` (D2 2026-08-20 -> 08-25 -> 09-09 -> 09-20) is a measurement series W2 reads — the source of record for W2's post-event trajectory series under its **STILL DO** cohort-level bullet — and no other routine has a step that reads it (corrected 2026-10-19, interactive owner session triaging the 2026-10-19 alert emails: this sentence said "W2 and W5 read", a reader list carried over unverified from the originating notice's own message; measured 2026-10-19, no W5 step reads the series — W5's only `Watchlist.md` steps mirror and reconcile queue membership against `events.decision_log`, and its one contact with the series was SPEC-DEFECT NOTICE INTAKE adjudicating the notice about it on 2026-10-11, which is adjudication, not a read of the measurements; do NOT add a W5 consumer on the strength of the old wording), but until now it was an EMERGENT, UNWRITTEN practice: this item said only add/remove/demote, so a run with no removes had no prompt-level reason to look at expiries, and skipping was silent — eighteen windows that closed 2026-08-31..09-04 went unannotated, a three-week hole. **THE RULE: every run, after the add/remove/demote pass, select the index rows in `Watchlist.md`'s "Strategy B new-entry candidates" section whose window-close date is `<=` the operating date and which carry no closing annotation, and for each record the post-window drift measured off IBKR RTH daily bars (window-close close vs event-day close, the same two-price convention as the index row) in a dated `CLOSED-WINDOW COHORT NOTE — UPDATE`, naming tickers explicitly (never positionally) and stating whether the closings are independent observations or one cohort.** A run that finds none states "no unannotated closed windows" in its `<note>`. Historical gaps are in scope: an unannotated closed window older than the catch-up evidence window is still annotated (oldest first, at most ten per run, remainder carried to the next run's `<note>` with the count, and that count plus the next-oldest window-close date also stated in the dated `CLOSED-WINDOW COHORT NOTE — UPDATE` itself, which W2 copies them from) rather than skipped as "prior runs' work"; if bars for a row cannot be retrieved, annotate it `UNMEASURED (<reason>)` so the series records the hole instead of hiding it. Annotation is state-index bookkeeping only: no scheduled action, no criterion re-derived.

4. ROUTER REVIEWS RECOMMENDED. An out-of-cycle `FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS` `as_of_date` newer than the standing monthly snapshot is ANSWERED once an `events.decision_log` `router-review` entry carries `fields.fundamental_axis_as_of` equal to it; skip answered dates. A D1 router_review flag meeting the qualifying geopolitical/resolution checks below takes REFRESH-ONLY, with no materiality review. For any other D1 flag apply Strategy.md's high inter-monthly material-regime-shift bar; if unmet, record the second-look decision in `events.decision_log` via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` and stop. EVERY-RUN duties already ran before STEP 1: (i) unserviced measured triggers, (ii) unanswered out-of-cycle FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS dates, and DAILY TECHNICAL-FLIP DIVERGENCE; do not repeat them here. After a D1-flag review writes CALL ROW, run FLIP CONSEQUENCES on a class change, then re-run the daily clause ONLY for that strategy. Its halt supersedes only still-pending items, never this run's drained/staged items; A-drain waits next STEP 1. A qualifying geopolitical/resolution flag takes REFRESH-ONLY below, no review; other flags take confirmed branch under NO SAME-RUN RE-RAISE.
   - **A SCORED OUT-OF-CYCLE FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS CHANGE.** For each as_of_date newer than standing monthly snapshot, log exactly ONE router-review entry with fields.fundamental_axis_as_of equal to it; one-line NO-CHANGE if no reconciliation-rule input moved. A moved input ALREADY meets materiality: queue affected review(s), go directly confirmed branch, no second discretion. M1R scores blind; this is the ONLY route from shock-axis triggers into activation in both directions. No new writer; same-evening D2 applies changed axes subject to NO SAME-RUN RE-RAISE (CALL ROW may still record remap).
   - **A MEASURED OUT-OF-CYCLE REFRESH TRIGGER ALSO MEETS THE BAR — DETECT EVERY RUN, BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Any ONE Strategy.md scenario 1/3 trigger requires refresh. Technical-plane de-risking: vix_regime_high, spy_trend_down, breadth_mom_drop_gt10, vix_drift_gt5_ending_normal; mirrors: vix_regime_exit_high, spy_trend_exit_down, breadth_mom_rise_gt10, vix_drift_down_gt5. Shock-axis refresh-only: shock_price_leg_entry/geopolitical_qualifying_event de-risk, shock_price_leg_exit/geopolitical_qualifying_resolution re-risk. Retired three-leg limb/asymmetry never gates them.
     - **DETECT** after dependency gate each run; completion does not prove step 1e succeeded. Read latest_as_of and state in the router-review entry if older than the last completed session. No today filter: missed-day triggers are caught only WHILE still holding, not replayed after ending. Use verbatim:
       `WITH re AS (SELECT scope, key, as_of_date, value, CAST(numeric_value AS FLOAT64) AS num FROM events.regime_events WHERE (scope = 'TECHNICAL_SIGNAL' AND key IN ('VIX_REGIME', 'SPY_TREND')) OR (scope = 'TECHNICAL_INPUT' AND key = 'EQUITY_BREADTH_PCT') QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY scope, key, as_of_date ORDER BY event_ts DESC, event_id DESC) = 1), lookback AS (SELECT x1.key, x1.as_of_date AS d, x1.value, x0.value AS start_value, x1.num - x0.num AS delta FROM re x1 JOIN re x0 ON x0.key = x1.key AND x0.as_of_date <= IF(x1.key = 'EQUITY_BREADTH_PCT', DATE_SUB(x1.as_of_date, INTERVAL 1 MONTH), DATE_SUB(x1.as_of_date, INTERVAL 30 DAY)) WHERE x1.key IN ('EQUITY_BREADTH_PCT', 'VIX_REGIME') QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY x1.key, x1.as_of_date ORDER BY x0.as_of_date DESC) = 1), leg0 AS (SELECT mark_date, shock_overlay_state, price_leg_elevated, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY mark_date) AS rn, COALESCE(NOT price_leg_elevated AND LOGICAL_OR(price_leg_elevated) OVER (ORDER BY mark_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING), FALSE) AS exit_cond, COALESCE(price_leg_elevated, FALSE) AS entry_cond FROM state.shock_price_leg_status), leg AS (SELECT *, MAX(IF(NOT exit_cond, rn, NULL)) OVER (ORDER BY rn ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS exit_lq, MAX(IF(NOT entry_cond, rn, NULL)) OVER (ORDER BY rn ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS entry_lq FROM leg0), last_score AS (SELECT as_of_date AS s, event_ts AS ts FROM events.regime_events WHERE scope = 'FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS' AND key = 'shock_overlay' ORDER BY event_ts DESC, event_id DESC LIMIT 1), read_cap AS (SELECT MAX(m.mark_date) AS seen FROM state.signal_marks_curated m CROSS JOIN last_score ls WHERE m.ticker = 'BZUSD' AND m.ingest_ts <= ls.ts), score_row AS (SELECT p.rn AS srn FROM leg p CROSS JOIN last_score ls CROSS JOIN read_cap rc WHERE p.mark_date < ls.s AND p.mark_date <= rc.seen QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY p.mark_date DESC) = 1), daily AS (SELECT 'vix_regime_high' AS trigger_name, as_of_date AS d, COALESCE(value = 'HIGH', FALSE) AS hit FROM re WHERE key = 'VIX_REGIME' UNION ALL SELECT 'vix_regime_exit_high', as_of_date, COALESCE(value != 'HIGH' AND LOGICAL_OR(value = 'HIGH') OVER (ORDER BY as_of_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING), FALSE) FROM re WHERE key = 'VIX_REGIME' UNION ALL SELECT 'spy_trend_down', as_of_date, COALESCE(value = 'DOWN', FALSE) FROM re WHERE key = 'SPY_TREND' UNION ALL SELECT 'spy_trend_exit_down', as_of_date, COALESCE(value != 'DOWN' AND LOGICAL_OR(value = 'DOWN') OVER (ORDER BY as_of_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING), FALSE) FROM re WHERE key = 'SPY_TREND' UNION ALL SELECT 'breadth_mom_drop_gt10', d, COALESCE(delta < -10, FALSE) FROM lookback WHERE key = 'EQUITY_BREADTH_PCT' UNION ALL SELECT 'breadth_mom_rise_gt10', d, COALESCE(delta > 10, FALSE) FROM lookback WHERE key = 'EQUITY_BREADTH_PCT' UNION ALL SELECT 'vix_drift_gt5_ending_normal', d, COALESCE(delta > 5 AND value = 'NORMAL', FALSE) FROM lookback WHERE key = 'VIX_REGIME' UNION ALL SELECT 'vix_drift_down_gt5', d, COALESCE(delta < -5 AND value != 'HIGH' AND start_value != 'HIGH', FALSE) FROM lookback WHERE key = 'VIX_REGIME' UNION ALL SELECT 'shock_price_leg_entry', g.mark_date, g.entry_cond AND NOT COALESCE(COALESCE(g.entry_lq, 0) < sr.srn, FALSE) FROM leg g LEFT JOIN score_row sr ON TRUE WHERE g.shock_overlay_state = 'latent' UNION ALL SELECT 'shock_price_leg_exit', g.mark_date, g.exit_cond AND NOT COALESCE(COALESCE(g.exit_lq, 0) < sr.srn AND g.rn <= sr.srn + 9, FALSE) FROM leg g LEFT JOIN score_row sr ON TRUE WHERE g.shock_overlay_state = 'acute'), marked AS (SELECT *, MAX(IF(NOT hit, d, NULL)) OVER (PARTITION BY trigger_name) AS last_quiet, MAX(d) OVER (PARTITION BY trigger_name) AS latest_as_of FROM daily) SELECT trigger_name, MIN(d) AS trigger_run_start, ANY_VALUE(latest_as_of) AS latest_as_of FROM marked WHERE hit AND d > COALESCE(last_quiet, DATE '1900-01-01') GROUP BY trigger_name`
       Zero rows is steady state. Exit triggers require a prior HIGH/DOWN and run until next extreme; no prior extreme means no exit. Breadth mirrors use one-month >10-point deltas; VIX rise>5/30 days ends NORMAL (LOW start allowed), fall<-5 requires both endpoints outside HIGH. Price legs use state.shock_price_leg_status (`bigquery/263`), a refresh proxy, NEVER the grade: entry ELEVATED only under latent, exit NOT ELEVATED after an elevated row only under acute; none yields no rows. **THE SCORER READ SESSION** is latest BZUSD leg date STRICTLY BEFORE latest shock_overlay as_of_date AND stored (`ingest_ts<=event_ts`) when it was scored; keep BOTH bounds, event_ts/event_id latest scoring order. A restatement may move the read session earlier, toward firing. leg rn / last-quiet row determine run start. Entry run already read by scorer stays quiet; read exit run is quiet through srn+9, re-arms at srn+10 if still holding. ANY new run after read session fires immediately, including within that window. No score_row → suppress nothing. Suppressed sessions count quiet, giving re-arm a new run_start. Do not substitute a calendar 10-day clock or scorer write date for these session/storage bounds; proxy may fire conservatively because it cannot see FX/spread/event legs.
     - **SERVICED ONCE PER RUN, STATE-KEYED BOTH DIRECTIONS.** `SELECT entry_id FROM events.decision_log WHERE entry_type = 'router-review' AND JSON_VALUE(fields, '$.measured_trigger') = '<trigger_name>' AND SAFE_CAST(JSON_VALUE(fields, '$.trigger_run_start') AS DATE) >= DATE '<trigger_run_start as YYYY-MM-DD>'` found → skip; else service. ON OR AFTER tolerates restated/re-anchored starts moving earlier within the same current run. Mirror names remain distinct keys. D1 flags below dedup by event date instead.
     - **SERVICE — TECHNICAL PLANE ONLY.** Four shock triggers read NO scope, run NO review, write NO activation/held/divergence/call row: REFRESH-ONLY LOG, D2a queues blind score, and scored-axis branch applies any moved axis. For technical triggers read state.current_regime STRATEGY_ACTIVATION ONCE BEFORE reviews write. Scope uses `COALESCE(UPPER(value) LIKE '%DO-NOT-ACTIVATE%', FALSE)`, including held suffix: de-risk every roster strategy failing it, re-risk every strategy passing it. Both directions → de-risk FIRST; same-direction triggers share review but each gets LOG entry. Exclude strategies lowered earlier this run from re-risk scope. An open divergence-review does not exclude a strategy: judged CALL ROW supersedes it. For each scoped strategy evaluate own Router activation rule from latest TECHNICAL_SIGNAL and BREADTH LEG FRESHER THAN ITS SIGNAL, then confirmed branch with rails:
       - **DE-RISKING:** (1) technical DO-NOT-ACTIVATE + conditional/ambiguous fundamental → DO-NOT-ACTIVATE. (2) technical DO-NOT-ACTIVATE but review would keep active → no in-session resolution; enqueue divergence-review per M4 sectionB Required fields, artifact standing Monthly_Fundamental.md, technical_reading latest signals, trigger_context trigger/run-start/FULL review reasoning, payload trigger_class measured-trigger plus standing fundamental_call/fundamental_call_entry_id/fundamental_cycle_as_of. If already open in state.open_queue_detail, no second; name it in entry. Re-check immediately BEFORE INSERT. Key `div-<CODE>-<YYYYMM of today>-<seq>` where seq=max historical prefix seq+1, never guessed 1. AFTER INSERT re-read and write held state only if this is strategy's ONLY open review (race → none, name both), per M4 HELD-STATE CONVENTION ON A DIVERGENCE-ATTACHED FLIP, as_of_date state.trading_day_today.today. A held row is not judged and gets NO CALL ROW.
       - **RE-RISKING, rails(1r)–(3r):** (1r) never ACTIVATE against own technical DO-NOT-ACTIVATE; ambiguous/conditional re-engage counts DO-NOT-ACTIVATE and writes nothing. (2r) never ACTIVATE against ANY standing reconciliation override (latest FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS per key): acute shock uses `SELECT strategy_code, override_applies FROM state.shock_transmission_status`, TRUE OR missing row binds; stressed risk_sentiment, decelerating growth+hawkish policy, reaccelerating inflation+hawkish policy apply exactly to M1b step 2's named strategies. Overrides only lower; only re-scored axes can lift them. (3r) technical ACTIVATE/no override but standing fundamental DO-NOT-ACTIVATE → enqueue EXACT pin(2) path and prior-state held row `DO-NOT-ACTIVATE — PENDING div-…`, no in-session raise. This includes d2-router-review protective calls daily clause excludes. Only technical ACTIVATE + no override + standing fundamental ACTIVATE permits confirmed in-session ACTIVATE, CALL ROW and FLIP CONSEQUENCES.
     - **NO SAME-RUN RE-RAISE.** LOWERED means an earlier THIS-run router-review LOG (technical de-risk or general D1 flag) moved operative ACTIVATE to DO-NOT-ACTIVATE, not a held prior-state suffix. EVERY later raise holds it at DO-NOT-ACTIVATE, writes no activation and names strategy/blocked write in own entry or note: SERVICE re-risk, scored-axis confirmed branch, daily mechanical agreement/reapply and general D1 flags all bind. A scored-axis CALL ROW may still record remap/reason; daily clause can enqueue resulting divergence this run, but agreement's mechanical raise waits next run.
     - **LOG OUT-OF-CYCLE, including empty scope / refresh-only.** ONE `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` per serviced trigger, entry_type router-review, strategy NULL. Technical tags router-review/out-of-cycle/measured-trigger/D2; fields measured_trigger,trigger_direction,trigger_run_start plain YYYY-MM-DD (also fundamental_axis_as_of form),latest_as_of, scoped strategies and per-strategy technical leg/fundamental call/outcome/divergence_id. Empty scope → NO-CHANGE. Shock tags add refresh-only; `fields` only `measured_trigger`, `trigger_direction`, `trigger_run_start`, `latest_as_of` (D1 flag = Daily snapshot date); no strategy/scope/call/outcome, reason awaits blind score. D2a reads ONLY measured_trigger/run_start.
     - **D1 GEOPOLITICAL FLAG:** verify dated Qualifying shock event per Rev 52 rubric/M1a HOW A SHOCK QUALIFYING EVENT IS DATED (named channel, not relief, window may be PENDING) AND standing shock_overlay NOT acute, not materiality. ~~Then take the SERVICE path above with `measured_trigger = 'geopolitical_qualifying_event'` and `trigger_run_start` = the event date.~~ Instead REFRESH-ONLY LOG `measured_trigger='geopolitical_qualifying_event'`, `trigger_direction='de-risking'`, `trigger_run_start` = event date; no review/scope/state/call write. Existing same measured_trigger/event date skips. Failed qualification/standing gate takes general D1 review.
     - **D1 RESOLUTION FLAG:** verify Rev 52 Qualifying resolution event (reverse category 4/named-channel attribution) AND standing shock_overlay is one of acute/latent; LOG `measured_trigger='geopolitical_qualifying_resolution'`, `trigger_direction='re-risking'`, `trigger_run_start` = event date, otherwise exactly same refresh-only/dedup path. Failure takes general review; lower shock reaches activation only via scored-axis change.
     - **LIMITS:** neither same-evening technical review nor shock refresh-only entry scores FUNDAMENTAL_AXIS or queues PENDING_REGIME_REFRESH. D2a alone converts logs to blind M1R refresh, scored next morning, applied D2 that evening; shocks have only that road. ^VIX/BZUSD let scorer use fresh shock evidence while macro remains monthly. No new activation writer.
   - **PRIMARY MACRO RELEASE contradicting standing growth_momentum/inflation_trend:** review via D1 REGIME CHECK here; no missing-detector referral or regime-refresh trigger. M1R cannot ingest that print, and shared monthly axes/one-way overrides deliberately remain until next M1a; do not inject evidence into blind queue. Log release in own router-review entry, no OUT-OF-SCOPE FINDINGS row. All five axes in any M1a/M1R snapshot share that snapshot, so lifting acute does not create a new stale-axis defect.
   - **CONFIRMED BRANCH.** In-session assess Daily development against state.current_regime and affected Strategy.md activation rules. Same operative class/scope with only annotation/PENDING suffix difference → NO-CHANGE, no state/CALL ROW. Else write `events.regime_events` scope `STRATEGY_ACTIVATION`, `as_of_date=state.trading_day_today.today` (never trigger/axis/onset), `source_review_ref='D2 router-review'` (D2-prefix excluded from bound reads), plus an `events.decision_log` review. **CALL ROW:** whenever judged state writes, even same class as standing call, record decided fundamental-call; not for held rows. On a re-scored axis, never write ACTIVATE while the strategy's own technical line reads DO-NOT-ACTIVATE. When this guard or NO SAME-RUN RE-RAISE blocks a remap differing from the standing call, record the re-mapped CALL ROW only and leave the divergence to the daily clause that same evening. Measured-trigger/D1 NO-CHANGE writes NO CALL ROW. Template verbatim:
     `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(<today>, 'fundamental-call', '<CODE>', NULL, '<ACTIVATE|DO-NOT-ACTIVATE>', NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, 'D2 <YYYY-MM-DD> standing fundamental call - <CODE>', '<reason>', TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT('<CODE>' AS strategy, 'd2-router-review' AS source_kind, '<cycle_as_of of the standing call this row amends, the artifact cycle for a transitional one; never today>' AS cycle_as_of, CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS raw_call, '<ACTIVATE|DO-NOT-ACTIVATE>' AS reconciled_call, <NULL or the scope restriction> AS call_qualifier, '<measured trigger | re-scored axis | D1 flag>' AS reconciliation_rule, <the standing call's fallback_suppressed> AS fallback_suppressed, '<technical call read this run>' AS technical_call_at_m1b, '<its as_of YYYY-MM-DD>' AS technical_as_of_at_m1b, <TRUE|FALSE> AS divergence_at_m1b, 'Monthly_Fundamental.md' AS m1b_artifact_path, '<40-char SHA or unverified>' AS m1b_artifact_commit, '<reason>' AS reason, '<entry_id>' AS review_entry_id)), ['Monthly_Fundamental.md@<40-char SHA or unverified>'], ['fundamental-call','standing-call','D2'], NULL, '<session>')`
     Amend STANDING cycle_as_of (artifact cycle transitional), never today; next M4 cycle outranks. Artifact commit follows HISTORY-DEPTH PRECHECK/transitional rule. Write review entry FIRST and put its id in review_entry_id. New call makes open old-call review SUPERSEDED, prior verdict out-of-cycle and daily comparison use new call. No calendar event. *(History: `ops/plan_history/D2.md` § H-D2-06.)*

5. STRATEGY TERMINATIONS. For each strategy flagged by D1's per-strategy kill-trigger sweep (or by a drained foundation-change assessment with a "terminate" verdict, or an Orchestrator m2m-termination TERMINATE verdict):
   - **DRAWDOWN termination (immediate, mechanical) / foundation-terminate / m2m-terminate:** execute the termination per Experiment_Parameters.md "Strategy termination and capital redistribution" — **TRADING-ENABLE RE-CHECK — SCOPED TO THE ORDER CRAFT ONLY, apply BEFORE crafting:** if the `state.trading_enabled` verdict carried forward from this routine's TRADING-ENABLE GATE reads FALSE, do NOT craft and do NOT write an `ORDER_STAGED` row for this termination — record that via `CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)` citing `halt_reason`, and carry the un-staged close forward to the next session, which re-checks the gate the same way. **What still runs regardless of the verdict:** marking the strategy TERMINATED, the termination-close escalation alert, and the post-mortem enqueue. Those are risk-RECORDING, not capital movement, and a kill trigger that has ALREADY fired must be recorded when it fires — otherwise a dead strategy stays silently marked active and keeps attracting sizing. **What DEFERS together with the craft:** the capital redistribution. It is not independent bookkeeping — it moves the terminated strategy's booked allocation to the survivors via `events.cash_flows`, and doing that while the positions are still open would zero the allocation of a strategy that still holds real exposure, corrupting per-strategy NAV and letting the survivors size against capital that is not actually free. Redistribute only once the close orders have actually been staged and reconciled; until then the termination is RECORDED and the capital simply stays put.  Then — stage exit orders to close ALL the strategy's open positions (connector-crafted — `create_order_instruction`'s own IBKR notification is the human-facing surface; `order_type='MARKET'`; a non-craftable position additionally gets a manual-entry `[Claude] Confirm order` event). **TERMINATION-CLOSE ESCALATION — for EACH close order staged in this step, immediately (same session, before moving on):** `CALL ops.sp_raise_alert('critical','D2','termination_close_staged', '<strategy> DRAWDOWN termination close — <ticker> <SIDE> <QTY> — CONFIRM IMMEDIATELY', '<JSON: strategy, ticker, instruction_id, trigger=drawdown>')`. Unlike a routine entry/exit (which relies solely on IBKR's own one-shot push notification), a termination-close order is urgent from hour 1 — this alert stays unresolved until D2a's Step 0 fill reconciliation confirms the close (see that step) and is re-emailed on every `alert_emailer.gs` poll while unresolved (not the normal notify-once behavior), not merely the next time D3's window-close check would otherwise catch a stale unfilled order days later. Mark the strategy **terminated** via an `events.regime_events` (scope `STRATEGY_ACTIVATION`) row (active→terminated; new entries blocked), write a TERMINATED `events.strategy_lifecycle` row (`to_state='TERMINATED'`, driver_routine='D2', **and `from_state` = the strategy's `state.strategy_roster.current_state` read immediately before this write — required because SL5 derives `CONCAT(strategy_code, ':', from_state, '->TERMINATED')`, whose NULL result would defeat discovery idempotency and violate `ops.roster_change_log.change_key STRING NOT NULL`. Never hardcode `'ADOPTED'`: a probe-stuck kill terminates from `PROBE` and a kill routed here from SL4's retirement path terminates from `RETIREMENT_PROPOSED`. AR_orc's strategy-retirement KEEP path already pins `from_state='RETIREMENT_PROPOSED'` explicitly, so pinning it here is this document's existing convention, not a new one**) and enqueue an SL2 `post-mortem` PENDING_DRAFT item **per the `PENDING_DRAFT` LANE CONTRACT in §SL2 — which pins `item_key='postmortem-<CODE>-<retired_date>'`, `status='pending'`, and `due_date` = the next Denver calendar day after `state.trading_day_today.today`; `trigger_context` is `payload.trigger_context`, not a column** (`events.queue_events`, item_type='post-mortem') so SL2 authors `events.strategy_postmortems` (the restart precondition), and once the closes reconcile (D2 Step 0), perform the **redistribution**: read `state.strategy_probe_funding_gap` (`bigquery/62_probe_stake_funding.sql`) `ORDER BY probe_entry_ts ASC`; for each row with `funding_gap_dollars > 0`, `strategy`-tag that much of the redistributed capital to it via `events.cash_flows` (FIFO, oldest `probe_entry_ts` first, one filled to its floor before the next) exactly per Operating_Protocols.md §13.C's "PENDING-NEWCOMER FIRST CLAIM" rule; then make the **AI CAPITAL-ALLOCATION CALL** (Operating_Protocols.md §16; `AI_DECISION_REDESIGN.md` §3 Redesign A) on the remainder among the active survivors read from `state.strategy_roster` (the as-of-flow-date roster, not a `/5` literal) — structured per-survivor `allocations` (array of `{strategy_code, pct, dollars}`, `pct` summing to 100), `conviction`/`conviction_pct`, a `rationale` naming why the top-allocated survivor (`winner_code`) beats the runner-up (`runner_up_code`), `invalidation`, `theater_check`. **RAILS (canonical text: Operating_Protocols.md §16 — on any wording divergence, §16 governs):** fit the call to the **[0.5×, 2×]-of-equal-share band per §16's fixed clamp-and-redistribute algorithm** (clamp out-of-band shares to the nearest edge, redistribute proportionally across UNCLAMPED shares only, repeat to convergence; assert `SUM(dollars) = remainder ± $0.01`); **below MEDIUM conviction, on a HOLD/no-call, or on any rail failure → DEFAULT-EQUAL**. Land the capital via **§16's termination double-entry**: one `strategy`-tagged **negative** `events.cash_flows` row for the terminated strategy and one `strategy`-tagged **positive** row per recipient, same flow_date, **every row tagged `source='termination_redistribution'`** (`bigquery/163`; unset source triggers `state.cash_flow_source_unknown`) (account-level `SUM(amount)` unchanged — an internal transfer; `analytics.strategy_nav` moves each survivor's NAV/2%-sizing base mechanically — this supersedes the former "reconcile in the events-side state" phrasing, 2026-07-19 review F2). Write an `events.decision_log` entry (`CALL ops.sp_log_decision(...)`, `entry_type='capital-allocation'`, `fields` JSON carrying `{trigger:'termination', allocations, conviction, conviction_pct, is_default_equal, winner_code, runner_up_code, total_dollars, invalidation, theater_check}` — surfaced on `state.capital_allocation_calls`, `bigquery/95_capital_allocator.sql`) recording the per-survivor redistribution amounts + any newcomer fills (the structured post-mortem itself is authored by SL2 from the enqueued item, not inline here); SL5 deregisters the roster row on the TERMINATED transition (roster fanout + CI checks). The drawdown trigger is rigid — do not wait on any review; the capital-allocation call itself is same-session and never a review either.
   - **RUNAWAY-SUCCESS flag:** do NOT terminate. Enqueue a `PENDING_REVIEW` entry (`INSERT INTO events.queue_events`, queue='PENDING_REVIEW'; review_type m2m-termination; the strategy; trigger_context = "runaway-success — deployed TWR doubled pre-gate; rule out reward-function exploitation / hidden tail risk per Experiment_Parameters.md kill-trigger #3"; attacker_due_date = next trading day; orchestrator_due_date = +1 trading day; status pending). The Attacker/Orchestrator routines adjudicate terminate-vs-continue and, on TERMINATE, execute the same termination + redistribution inline. *(Pre-2026-10-30 history and evidence for this rule: `ops/plan_history/D2.md` § H-D2-07.)*

6. PARK ALLOCATION CONVERSION — **RETIRED 2026-10-15 by owner directive** (`bigquery/256_park_voo_only.sql`; Operating_Protocols.md §13.F). The park is VOO-only and D1 no longer makes a park call, so there is nothing to convert: do NOT read `state.park_allocation_latest`, do NOT write `events.park_policy_changes`, and do NOT craft a park switch leg. `state.park_menu` is VOO-only, so any conversion into another vehicle fails the menu-membership rail regardless. Idle-cash sweeps into VOO, covers out of VOO, and the stranded-leg sale of any non-VOO park holding stay in Operating_Protocols.md §13.E, executed by D2a. DEFERRAL DISCIPLINE: if a decision genuinely cannot be resolved this routine, specify (a) the trigger date and information source that will resolve it, and (b) the conservative-default fallback (skip / decline / exit). Deferrals do not chain. Enqueue a `PENDING_ANALYSIS` entry (`INSERT INTO events.queue_events`; due_date = the resolution date) so D2 drains it then — do not create a calendar event for analysis.

CALENDAR MCP USAGE: Claude calls the Calendar MCP directly only for a non-craftable order's manual-entry `[Claude] Confirm order` event, or a BigQuery-unreachable `[Claude] ATTENTION — RE-AUTH` event (2026-07-09 — craftable orders and ordinary hard-stops rely on IBKR's own notification / `alert_emailer.gs` instead). Time zone per Experiment_Parameters.md (default America/Denver if silent). Set per-event notification to fire at event-time.

CHAT OUTPUT (per chat output discipline):
- Order(s) to execute as crafted instructions (tap-to-confirm deep link + `SIDE QTY TICKER TYPE LIMIT TIF` summary), grouped by execution day if more than one. Use "no order" if no exits staged. If Step 0 reconciled fills, state it in one line.
- One-line acknowledgment of writes and calendar events created (e.g., "events.decision_log + events.position_events written, Watchlist.md updated. 1 order instruction crafted, 1 calendar event scheduled.").

If no orders, no file changes, no events: "No actions required."
